open: In the name of Allah. Assalamu alaikum, my dears. Come closer, tonight’s story is very beautiful.
s1a: Noah… Ilyas… Have you ever been really sick? With a high fever, and you had to stay in bed for days?
s1b: Yes! It was sooo boring. And my throat hurt so much!
s1c: Oh, my dear. Get warm and cosy… Today I’ll tell you about a prophet who wasn’t sick for just a few days, but for many, many years: the Prophet Ayyub, peace be upon him.
s2a: Allah had given Ayyub a family and many good things. And Ayyub worshipped Allah sincerely. Then came a great test. Ayyub lost much of what he loved. And he became very sick, very sick indeed, so that for many long years he was not healed.
s2b: Many long years? Why does Allah let a prophet be so sick?
s2c: That is a very good question, my dear. Our Prophet Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him, said: The people most severely tested are the prophets. And he said: The greatness of the reward comes with the greatness of the trial, and when Allah loves a people, He tests them. That means: whoever is patient gets a great reward. And he also said: No tiredness and no illness befalls a Muslim without Allah wiping away some of his sins through it.
s3a: Most people stayed away from Ayyub. Only very few still came to him, and his wife took care of him.
s3b: That’s not nice at all! Why didn’t anyone visit him?
s3c: Yes, my dear. That is why we should visit the sick. Our Prophet told us that Allah will say on the Day of Resurrection: O son of Adam, I was sick and you did not visit Me. The person will say: O my Lord, how could I visit You, when You are the Lord of the worlds? Allah will say: My servant so-and-so was sick and you did not visit him. Did you not know that if you had visited him, you would have found Me with him?
s3d: And Ayyub? Did he never complain?
s3e: Ayyub stayed patient. Allah says about him in the Qur’an: “Indeed, We found him patient, an excellent servant. Indeed, he was one repeatedly turning back to Allah.” That means: he always turned back to Allah. He did not complain to people, but he asked Allah for help, with a very beautiful prayer.
s4a: Ayyub called to his Lord: “Indeed, adversity has touched me, and You are the Most Merciful of the merciful.” Do you hear how polite that is? He didn’t say: Heal me right now! He only told Allah what was hurting him, and he mentioned Allah’s mercy.
s4b: That’s a beautiful dua! Can I say it too when I’m sick?
s4c: Of course, my dear! It is a prayer from the Qur’an. Everyone may say it.
s5a: And Allah answered Ayyub’s prayer! Allah said to him: “Strike the ground with your foot; this is a spring for a cool bath and drink.” That means: stamp on the ground with your foot! And a spring burst out of the earth! Cool water for washing and for drinking.
s5b: Ayyub washed and drank, and Allah took the illness away from him. Ayyub was healthy again! And Allah gave him back his family, and the like thereof with them, “as mercy from Us and a reminder for the worshippers”.
s6a: And our Prophet Muhammad told us another beautiful thing about Ayyub. Later, while Ayyub was washing, locusts of gold fell on him, all made of gold! And Ayyub began scooping them with his hands into his garment.
s6c: Then his Lord called him: O Ayyub, have I not made you rich enough to need nothing of what you see? Ayyub said: Yes indeed, by Your might, my Lord! But I can never do without Your blessing.
s7a: Oh… they’ve fallen asleep. My dears… when you are sick or tired, be patient like Ayyub. Say his beautiful prayer: My Lord, adversity has touched me, and You are the Most Merciful of the merciful. Visit people who are sick. And when you are healthy, say: Alhamdulillah.
s7b: And next time, I’ll tell you about Shuaib… and about people who cheated with measure and weight. And you, watching us right now: if you liked the story, ask your parents to subscribe to our channel, so you don’t miss the next story.
close: And you, dear fathers and mothers: subscribe to our channel, and share these stories with the people you love, so that together we pass on the beautiful message of Islam to our children.
final: Good night, my dears. I entrust you to Allah, with whom nothing entrusted is ever lost.
